articles.title: Bovine Colostrum Is the Latest Gut Health Obsession. Your Grandmother Called It Kharvas and Ate It Decades Ago.
articles.excerpt: TikTok influencers are spending $50 a tub on what Indian families have been eating for generations. The science is finally catching up — but it is more complicated than the wellness industry wants you to believe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mosquitoes Can Learn to Love the Smell of DEET. If You Are Visiting India This Summer, Read This.
articles.excerpt: A new study in the Journal of Experimental Biology found that after just three exposures, 60 per cent of mosquitoes tried to bite the hand covered in repellent. For NRIs heading into monsoon season, the timing could not be worse.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The American Heart Association Just Said Exercise Protects Your Heart Even if You Never Lose Weight. South Asians Need to Hear This.
articles.excerpt: A landmark scientific statement in Circulation says physical activity reduces cardiovascular risk independent of the scale. For a community with the highest heart disease rates in the country, the implications are urgent.

sources.label: AHA 2026 Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Four Adults With a 'Normal' BMI Are Actually Obese. For South Asians, the Numbers Are Worse.
articles.excerpt: A USC study of 5,642 Americans found that BMI misses dangerous hidden fat. For a community that develops diabetes and heart disease at lower body weights, this is a wake-up call.

sources.label: WHO Expert Consultation on BMI in Asian Populations (2004)

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Medicare Will Cover Wegovy and Zepbound for $50 a Month Starting July 1. If Your Parents Are on Medicare, Read This.
articles.excerpt: The new GLP-1 Bridge program opens weight-loss drug access to 14 million Medicare beneficiaries. For NRI families managing ageing parents' health from abroad, the financial and logistical implications are substantial.
articles.nri_angle: Many NRI families have elderly parents on Medicare. South Asians face higher visceral fat accumulation and metabolic syndrome at lower BMIs. The $50 GLP-1 programme directly impacts diaspora families managing elder care remotely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The FDA Just Approved the First Needle-Free Insulin for Children. For South Asian Families Managing Diabetes, It Changes Everything.
articles.excerpt: MannKind's Afrezza, an inhaled rapid-acting insulin, is now cleared for kids aged six and older. With 350,000 American children living with diabetes and South Asians facing some of the highest rates in the world, this is not a niche approval.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face disproportionately high rates of diabetes, including growing Type 2 incidence in adolescents. A needle-free insulin option reduces adherence barriers for diaspora families managing children's diabetes across school, sports, and social settings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gas Prices Have Jumped 42 Per Cent in One Year. American Drivers Will Pay $700 More. Immigrant Families Are Absorbing the Worst of It.
articles.excerpt: The national average has hit $4.33 a gallon, with California above $6. For NRI households already stretched between remittances, tuition, and groceries, this summer at the pump will be the most expensive in recent memory.

sources.label: iSeeCars / Karl Brauer — Annual war penalty study
Reuters — US gasoline market stock draws
Autoblog — Gas prices cost drivers $700 more

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 10-Second Video of Your Eyes Can Now Detect Iron Deficiency Without a Blood Test. South Asian Women Should Be Paying Attention.
articles.excerpt: Israeli researchers built a needle-free test that spots anaemia by analysing blood vessels in the whites of your eyes. For a community where half of all women are iron-deficient, this could change how millions get screened.

sources.label: Clinical trial — 224-participant Israeli study on conjunctival vessel analysis
Dr Peter Campbell, Oregon Health & Science University

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Review of the Evidence Says a Simple Eating Schedule Can Prevent Diabetes. South Asians Should Read It Twice.
articles.excerpt: Researchers found that limiting meals to a consistent daily window — and avoiding food after dark — reduces the risk of obesity and type 2 diabetes. For a community where 30 per cent develop prediabetes by 45, the timing may matter more than the menu.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American Summers Are Getting Dangerously Hotter. If You Have South Asian Genes, Your Heart Is Already at Higher Risk.
articles.excerpt: A new study projects a 34 per cent rise in heat-related cardiovascular disease by 2050 — driven by warming and ageing demographics. For a community with elevated baseline cardiac risk, the overlap is alarming.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Announced the Theme for Yoga Day 2026. It Is Aimed Squarely at Your Ageing Parents.
articles.excerpt: The 12th International Day of Yoga will focus on 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing' as India's senior population surges past 150 million. For diaspora families managing elder care from thousands of miles away, the timing could not be better.

sources.label: Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Red Light Therapy Masks Are Everywhere on Social Media. Dermatologists Say the Science Is Real but the Marketing Is Not.
articles.excerpt: At-home LED devices promise everything from wrinkle reduction to acne healing. A new wave of clinical evidence says some claims hold up — but South Asian skin types face specific risks that influencers never mention.

sources.label: Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Study of 600 People Found That Low B12 and Folate Levels Predict Chronic Fatigue. South Asian Vegetarians Are Among the Most Vulnerable.
articles.excerpt: Japanese researchers linked elevated homocysteine — a marker of B12 and folate deficiency — to persistent physical exhaustion in men and low motivation in women. The findings have direct implications for the millions of South Asians who follow plant-based diets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Drug Taken Before and After Prostate Surgery Made Patients Nine Times More Likely to Be Cancer-Free. The Study Just Changed the Standard of Care.
articles.excerpt: J&J's Erleada, given for six months before and after surgery, reduced the risk of the cancer spreading or death by 20 per cent. ASCO chose the data to open its plenary session.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Targeted Drug Just Doubled Survival for the Deadliest Form of Colorectal Cancer. South Asians Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: Pfizer's BRAFTOVI combination cut the risk of death by 44 per cent in patients with BRAF-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer — a subtype with one of the worst prognoses in oncology.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 25-Year Study of 32,000 People Found That Quitting Smoking Drops Dementia Risk to the Level of Someone Who Never Smoked.
articles.excerpt: The benefit kicks in after about seven years smoke-free. For South Asian families where elder male smoking is common, the findings are a wake-up call that it is never too late.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Major Scientific Review Just Found That Vaping Can Damage DNA and May Cause Cancer. South Asian Parents Need to Read This.
articles.excerpt: The review, published in Carcinogenesis, examined laboratory, animal, and human studies. The evidence links e-cigarette aerosols to cancers of the lung, mouth, and bladder.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Deadliest Heatwave in 28 Years Has Killed More Than 2,200 People. If You Have Family Back Home, Here Is What You Need to Know.
articles.excerpt: Roads have melted in Delhi. Temperatures hit 50°C. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana account for more than 80 per cent of the dead. Monsoon relief may still be weeks away.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Reserve Report Found That 10 Per Cent of American Households Do Not Have Enough Food. The Number Has Doubled Since 2020.
articles.excerpt: The savings rate has dropped to 2.6 per cent. More than a third of households are dipping into savings to cover daily expenses. For immigrant families balancing costs across two countries, the squeeze is compounding.
articles.nri_angle: NRI families face a unique dual-country financial squeeze: rising US costs (gas above $4, food inflation, rents) drain household budgets while remittance obligations to India remain fixed or growing. The savings rate collapse to 2.6% is especially dangerous for families maintaining financial commitments across two economies. Food insecurity compounds pre-existing South Asian cardiovascular and diabetes risks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A New Class of Cancer Drugs Delivers Radiation Directly to Tumours. ASCO 2026 Data Suggests It Could Replace Chemotherapy for Some Patients.
articles.excerpt: Radioligand therapies attach radioactive atoms to molecules that seek out cancer cells. The latest results against prostate cancer are the strongest yet — and the field now commands 40 per cent of Novartis's oncology R&D budget.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian men face higher rates of aggressive prostate cancer and tend to present at later stages due to lower screening rates and cultural stigma. Radioligand therapy's targeted, less toxic approach is especially relevant for this population, offering an alternative to chemotherapy with fewer side effects for older patients.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Chinese Cancer Drug Just Beat the Global Gold Standard for Lung Cancer. It Is the First From Asia to Earn a Plenary at ASCO in 61 Years.
articles.excerpt: Ivonescimab reduced the risk of death by 34 per cent in advanced squamous lung cancer. The results were published in The Lancet the same day. For Indian families watching air-pollution-driven cancer rates climb, the implications are significant.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The WHO Just Endorsed a $1 Antibiotic Pill That Prevents Syphilis and Chlamydia After Sex. It Is Their First Recommendation of Its Kind.
articles.excerpt: Doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis can reduce syphilis and chlamydia by up to 80 per cent. With STI rates rising sharply in India and across the diaspora, the decision could reshape sexual health prevention worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Asian Adults in the US Have 30 Per Cent Prediabetes by Age 45. They Also Report the Healthiest Diets. A Major Study Says the Paradox Is Real.
articles.excerpt: The MASALA study followed 2,700 adults for a decade and found that South Asians develop cardiovascular risk factors earlier than every other ethnic group — despite doing many of the right things.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Surgeon General Just Classified Youth Screen Time as a Public Health Crisis. More Than Half of Teens Are on Their Phones Past Midnight.
articles.excerpt: A new JAMA Pediatrics study found that 50 per cent of American teenagers spend up to an hour on their phones between 10 PM and 6 AM on school nights. The federal advisory calls for immediate parental action.

sources.label: US Department of Health and Human Services / Office of the Surgeon General

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Daily Pill Just Doubled Survival in Advanced Pancreatic Cancer. It Is the First Drug to Ever Do This.
articles.excerpt: Daraxonrasib cut the risk of death by 60 per cent in a 500-person trial. The results, presented at ASCO 2026 and published in the NEJM, are being called the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer in decades.

sources.label: The New England Journal of Medicine

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Study of 540,000 People Found That Exercise at Work Does Not Protect Your Health the Way Leisure Exercise Does. The Genetics Are Different.
articles.excerpt: A Nature Genetics study using data from the Million Veteran Program and UK Biobank found that leisure-time physical activity has distinct genetic pathways and uniquely protects against diabetes, heart failure and early death.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The FDA Just Approved Inhaled Insulin for Children. For South Asian Families Managing Diabetes, the Needle Era May Finally Be Ending.
articles.excerpt: Afrezza, the first needle-free mealtime insulin for kids aged six and above, costs $35 a month and mimics the body's natural insulin response more closely than injections do.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Drug That Blocks Cortisol Just Cut the Risk of Death From Ovarian Cancer by 35 Per Cent. No Biomarker Testing Was Required.
articles.excerpt: The Phase 3 ROSELLA trial found that adding the cortisol-blocking drug relacorilant to chemotherapy extended survival in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer patients — regardless of prior treatment history. The results, presented at ASCO 2026, could establish a new standard of care.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Head-to-Head Trial Found That One Prostate Cancer Drug Causes Half the Cognitive Decline of Another. Every Patient Who Switched Was on the Worse Drug.
articles.excerpt: The ARACOG trial, presented at ASCO 2026, is the first rigorous comparison of how two standard prostate cancer drugs affect memory, attention, and executive function. The results may change how doctors and families approach treatment decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Study of 139 Cancer Patients Found That Getting Immunotherapy in the Morning Cut Recurrence by 77 Per Cent. The Only Change Was the Clock.
articles.excerpt: Multiple ASCO 2026 presentations and a randomised trial in Nature Medicine now confirm that circadian timing of cancer treatment is not a footnote — it may be one of the most powerful free interventions in oncology.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated risks for several cancers including breast, oral, and stomach. Nearly five million Indian Americans navigate a healthcare system where treatment timing is assigned by clinic convenience, not biology. This zero-cost intervention — simply requesting a morning infusion slot — could meaningfully improve outcomes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mounjaro Outperformed Every Other GLP-1 Drug in a Two-Year Trial of Early Type 2 Diabetes Patients. 60 Per Cent Achieved Normal Blood Sugar.
articles.excerpt: The SURPASS-EARLY trial found that tirzepatide helped recently diagnosed patients reach glycaemic targets 4 to 12 weeks faster than semaglutide and produced sustained normal HbA1c levels in more than double the patients on competing drugs.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest type 2 diabetes rates globally — 23 per cent prevalence among Indian Americans vs 11 per cent in the general US population. They develop diabetes a decade earlier and at lower BMI thresholds, making early aggressive treatment even more critical. The SURPASS-EARLY data directly supports earlier intervention with tirzepatide for this population.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Studies Just Proved That Long COVID Neurological Symptoms Are Caused by the Body Attacking Itself. Existing Drugs May Already Work.
articles.excerpt: Autoantibodies from long COVID patients caused fatigue, pain, and nerve damage when transferred to healthy mice — even two years after infection. Researchers say millions could benefit from immunotherapy treatments already on the market.

sources.label: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

articles.nri_angle: India experienced one of the world's most severe COVID waves, with seroprevalence above 90 per cent by mid-2022. South Asians in the US, UK, and Canada report higher rates of post-COVID fatigue and cognitive complaints than the general population. The autoantibody finding offers a testable biomarker and a path to targeted treatment for millions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Just 10 Minutes of AI Use Can Measurably Weaken Your Problem-Solving Skills. A New Study Says the Damage May Compound Over Time.
articles.excerpt: Participants who asked ChatGPT for direct answers performed significantly worse when the tool was taken away. Those who used it for hints did not. The distinction matters for every knowledge worker in the diaspora.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans are the most tech-forward ethnic group in the US, with disproportionate representation in engineering, data science, and product management — exactly the roles where AI tools are most deeply embedded. The study's findings directly challenge the efficiency narrative that many diaspora professionals have built their careers around.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
